title: Minor Tectonic Plates
_note: Hand-maintained. `pb2002_name` keys into media/base/pb2002-plates.json; scripts/generate_tectonic_plate_maps.py renders one locator per plate.

concepts.name: Aegean Sea Plate
concepts.definition: The Aegean Sea Plate is a small plate of thinned continental crust beneath Greece, the Aegean Sea, and western Turkey that is being stretched westward as the African Plate subducts beneath it at the Hellenic Trench.

concepts.name: Altiplano Plate
concepts.definition: The Altiplano Plate is one of the 38 small plates in Peter Bird's PB2002 model, covering the high Andean plateau of southern Peru, Bolivia, and northern Chile; it has no dedicated Wikipedia article, appearing only as a redlink in the List of tectonic plates, since the region is really an orogen where plate boundaries are loosely defined.

concepts.name: Amur Plate
concepts.definition: The Amur Plate is a minor continental plate spanning northeastern China, the Korean Peninsula, and southwestern Japan that rotates slowly counterclockwise and is linked to significant regional seismicity.

concepts.name: Anatolia Plate
concepts.definition: The Anatolian Plate is a small continental plate carrying most of Turkey that is being extruded westward at about 21 mm/year between the North and East Anatolian Fault zones, among the most active transform faults on Earth.

concepts.name: Balmoral Reef Plate
concepts.definition: The Balmoral Reef Plate is a small oceanic microplate under the North Fiji Basin, north of Fiji, whose young seafloor (under 12 million years old) is spreading between the New Hebrides and Tonga subduction zones.

concepts.name: Banda Sea Plate
concepts.definition: The Banda Sea Plate is a small, seismically active plate in eastern Indonesia carrying parts of Sulawesi, Seram, and the Banda Islands, formed where the Australian Plate collides with and subducts beneath the Banda Arc.

concepts.name: Birds Head Plate
concepts.definition: The Bird's Head Plate is a small plate at the western tip of New Guinea, carrying the Bird's Head Peninsula, that has broken away from the Australian Plate and collides with the Caroline Plate to its north.

concepts.name: Burma Plate
concepts.definition: The Burma Plate is a small plate carrying the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and northwest Sumatra, formed as an island arc above the India Plate's subduction at the Sunda Trench, with the Andaman Sea spreading behind it.

concepts.name: Caroline Plate
concepts.definition: The Caroline Plate is a small oceanic plate straddling the equator north of New Guinea, containing the West and East Caroline Basins, that is being consumed by subduction beneath the Bird's Head Plate to its south.

concepts.name: Conway Reef Plate
concepts.definition: The Conway Reef Plate is a small oceanic microplate in the North Fiji Basin west of Fiji, wedged between the Central Spreading Ridge and West Fiji Ridge, rotating counterclockwise relative to all its neighbors.

concepts.name: Easter Plate
concepts.definition: The Easter Microplate is a small, fast-spreading oceanic plate west of Easter Island, wedged between the Nazca and Pacific Plates, with seafloor spreading rates up to 140 mm/year, among the highest recorded globally.

concepts.name: Futuna Plate
concepts.definition: The Futuna Plate is a very small oceanic microplate near Futuna Island in the southwest Pacific, squeezed between the Pacific and Australian Plates and adjoining the Niuafo'ou Plate.

concepts.name: Galapagos Plate
concepts.definition: The Galapagos Microplate is a tiny (about 13,000 km squared) oceanic plate in the eastern Pacific that accommodates the meeting of the Pacific, Cocos, and Nazca Plates at the Galapagos triple junction.

concepts.name: Juan Fernandez Plate
concepts.definition: The Juan Fernandez Plate is a small, clockwise-rotating oceanic microplate in the South Pacific that formed 3-4 million years ago at a triple junction with the Nazca, Antarctic, and Pacific Plates.

concepts.name: Kermadec Plate
concepts.definition: The Kermadec Plate is a long, narrow oceanic microplate north of New Zealand that overrides the subducting Pacific Plate at the Kermadec Trench, one of the most seismically active zones in the southwest Pacific.

concepts.name: Manus Plate
concepts.definition: The Manus Plate is a tiny, roughly 100-km-wide oceanic microplate northeast of New Guinea that rotates counterclockwise at one of the fastest rates of any plate on Earth, wedged between the North Bismarck and Pacific Plates.

concepts.name: Maoke Plate
concepts.definition: The Maoke Plate is a small plate underlying western New Guinea's Sudirman Range, home to Puncak Jaya, that moves north at roughly 70 mm/year relative to Africa amid complex, still-debated boundaries with surrounding plates.

concepts.name: Mariana Plate
concepts.definition: The Mariana Plate is a small oceanic plate west of the Mariana Trench that carries the Mariana Islands volcanic arc, formed above the subducting Pacific Plate with active back-arc spreading along its western edge.

concepts.name: Molucca Sea Plate
concepts.definition: The Molucca Sea Plate is a small, now fully subducted oceanic plate between Sulawesi and Halmahera in Indonesia, famous as the only known example of divergent double subduction, being consumed from both sides simultaneously.

concepts.name: New Hebrides Plate
concepts.definition: The New Hebrides Plate is a small plate carrying the island nation of Vanuatu, sitting above the Australian Plate's subduction at the New Hebrides Trench, one of the most seismically active margins in the Pacific.

concepts.name: Niuafo'ou Plate
concepts.definition: The Niuafo'ou Plate is a small, earthquake-prone oceanic microplate in the Lau Basin west of Tonga, riddled with active faults where it abuts the volatile Tonga Plate.

concepts.name: North Andes Plate
concepts.definition: The North Andes Plate is a small continental plate covering the northern Andes of Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela, compressed between the South American and Nazca Plates and marked by intense volcanic and seismic activity.

concepts.name: North Bismarck Plate
concepts.definition: The North Bismarck Plate is a small, now largely inactive or relic plate in the Bismarck Sea northeast of New Guinea, once host to the volcanoes of the Melanesian arc and separated from the South Bismarck Plate by a highly seismic fault zone.

concepts.name: Okhotsk Plate
concepts.definition: The Okhotsk Plate is a minor continental plate covering the Sea of Okhotsk region, Kamchatka, Sakhalin, the Kurils, and northern Japan, moving southwest as the Pacific Plate subducts beneath it and generates some of the world's largest earthquakes.

concepts.name: Okinawa Plate
concepts.definition: The Okinawa Plate is a small continental plate stretching from Taiwan to Kyushu that carries the Ryukyu Islands and is being deformed as the Philippine Sea Plate converges on its eastern edge, producing both earthquakes and slow-slip events.

concepts.name: Panama Plate
concepts.definition: The Panama Plate is a small plate carrying Costa Rica and Panama, sandwiched between actively spreading ridges and overriding the subducting Cocos and Nazca Plates to its south.

concepts.name: Rivera Plate
concepts.definition: The Rivera Plate is a small oceanic microplate off the west coast of Mexico, just south of Baja California, that subducts beneath the North American Plate and has caused some of the strongest earthquakes in Mexican history.

concepts.name: Sandwich Plate
concepts.definition: The South Sandwich Plate is a small oceanic microplate in the Southern Ocean carrying the South Sandwich Islands, formed above the subducting South American Plate and bounded by the Antarctic and Scotia Plates.

concepts.name: Shetland Plate
concepts.definition: The South Shetland Plate is a small oceanic microplate off the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, carrying the South Shetland Islands, that formed 3-4 million years ago through back-arc rifting and is bordered mostly by the Antarctic Plate.

concepts.name: Solomon Sea Plate
concepts.definition: The Solomon Sea Plate is a small oceanic plate east of Papua New Guinea that is being consumed by subduction beneath the South Bismarck and Pacific Plates at the highly active New Britain Trench.

concepts.name: South Bismarck Plate
concepts.definition: The South Bismarck Plate is a small plate in the southern Bismarck Sea carrying eastern New Guinea and New Britain, marked by high earthquake and volcanic activity where the Solomon Sea Plate subducts beneath it.

concepts.name: Timor Plate
concepts.definition: The Timor Plate is a small plate in Southeast Asia carrying the island of Timor, formed where the Australian Plate subducts beneath its southern edge and it converges with the Banda Sea Plate to the north.

concepts.name: Tonga Plate
concepts.definition: The Tonga Plate is a small, elongated oceanic microplate in the southwest Pacific that subducts the Pacific Plate along the Tonga Trench and rotates clockwise amid intense seismic activity.

concepts.name: Woodlark Plate
concepts.definition: The Woodlark Plate is a small, triangular oceanic microplate in the Woodlark Basin east of New Guinea, now understood via GPS data to be much smaller than once thought, being subducted beneath the New Georgia Islands to its east.

concepts.name: Yangtze Plate
concepts.definition: The Yangtze Plate is a minor continental plate underlying most of southern China that moves southeast at about 15 mm/year, rifting away from the Okinawa Plate to its east and colliding with the Eurasian Plate along the Longmenshan Fault to its west.
